confidence_notes: I based the restaurant meal, coffee and beer anchors on aggregated cost-of-living figures from mid-2026. Expatica's figures, which use Numbeo data from June 2026, were about £15.18 for an inexpensive meal, £3.65 for a cappuccino, £6.07 for a domestic draught beer and £70.82 for a three-course meal for two. CityCost's July 2026 figures were similar at about £15, £3.80 and £72. A few other sources gave lower prices, so these anchors could be off by around 15-20%. The cocktail (about £10) and wine (about £7) anchors are estimates based on how drink prices usually compare with beer in the UK, so they are less certain. I converted GBP to USD at an assumed rate of about 1.33, which I did not check against a source. The accommodation anchors are model estimates for July, which is summer peak season. I did not check any live listings for them. They could vary widely because of events like concerts and football matches.
comparable_city_reasoning: Large regional UK city. Prices are lower than London's and similar to Birmingham, Leeds and Liverpool.
